solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When carrier is out of place

parts.note: 'as' can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tray is something you carry things on

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the airline or postal carrier went missing or off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone astray has wandered off and ended up somewhere it does not belong.

clue.text: Trim chap set on one kipper

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it, so the first words come first

parts.note: a chap is a man
the Roman numeral for one
to kipper a herring is to cure it by salting and smoking

explanation.surface: A chap is perched on a single smoked herring, which is cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a British breakfast fish, a smoked herring; here the word is a verb meaning to preserve fish that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the hands in which the fingernails are trimmed and shaped.

clue.text: Steady's blooming prettiness

indicators.note: something blooming opens out and changes form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone's steady girlfriend has a flowering beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady' looks like a noun for a partner, but it is the adjective; ''s' is short for 'is' and links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent and steady both describe something that continues constantly without letting up.

clue.text: Secure new farm building

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A farmer secures a brand-new outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is the large shed on a farm used for storing grain, hay or animals.

clue.text: Sweet cracker wound up meal with first bit of Brie included

parts.note: a cracker, like a peach, is something excellent or a stunner

indicators.note: something included is put inside the other word
wound up suggests being twisted round, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of Brie

explanation.surface: A dessert spoils a meal that had cheese in it, with the cheese thrown in at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Brie's B goes into the letters of meal, and that group is then rearranged; 'cracker' is British slang for something excellent, as is 'peach'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a classic dessert of peaches, raspberry sauce and ice cream, so it is a sweet in the British sense of pudding.

clue.text: Head from boycott being full of energy

indicators.note: a word that is full of something holds it inside

parts.note: to boycott is to ban
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A headline: a head emerges from a boycott with plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' tempts as a company boss; it is slang for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal British slang for the head, as in 'use your bean' or 'a bean ball'.

clue.text: I will be included in latest decoration

indicators.note: something included in a word is placed inside it

parts.note: the final one is the latest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows they will feature in the newest ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is an ornamental knob or spike on top of a roof, post or bedstead.

clue.text: Glare met unsettling old message

indicators.note: unsettling the words disturbs their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disturbing communication was received with an angry stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a printed wire message, a now largely obsolete form of communication.

clue.text: Tired team struggles, there's no getting away from it

definitions.text: there's no getting away from it

parts.note: stale means tired and jaded

indicators.note: a team that struggles is thrown into disarray, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weary side is having a hard time and feels trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a stalemate leaves a player with no legal move, so more widely it is a deadlock with no way out.

clue.text: Pick some counsel I tender

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: found running across the end of counsel, the I and the start of tender

explanation.surface: A lawyer offers to pick out some of the advice he gives.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group, its best members, are its elite.

clue.text: Checks on popular shortcoming

parts.note: re means on or concerning
something in is fashionable or popular
a sin is a moral failing

explanation.surface: Someone checks up on a well-liked person's weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' is a verb, and the rest builds the answer in three small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or a habit is to restrain it, just as checking something holds it back.

clue.text: Restrict rook quite well

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle or con them
feeling fine is being quite well

explanation.surface: A chess player limits the rook, which is doing reasonably well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' suggests chess or R, but it is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine something is to keep it within limits, which is to restrict it.

clue.text: Second person is green but no good

indicators.note: but here means except, so what follows is left out

parts.note: green means inexperienced or young
NG is the common abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A runner-up is inexperienced and useless.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the second person is the form addressing the listener, which in English is this pronoun.

clue.text: Flatten mall and restore in a new way

indicators.note: doing something in a new way means the letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Developers knock down a shopping centre and rebuild it differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To steamroller something is to crush or flatten it, like the heavy roller levelling a road.

clue.text: Created in green Eden, I flourished

indicators.note: a flourish is a showy twirl, so these letters are swirled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A first-person creation story: made in the lush Garden of Eden, I thrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engineered has been designed and built, which is to say created.

clue.text: In two minds about the guard

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on art
taken as written
a fence is a barrier that guards a property

explanation.surface: Someone is undecided about the security guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting on the fence is an idiom for refusing to choose a side, being undecided.

clue.text: Question of place with that girl close to me

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
her is the pronoun for that girl

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of me

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where they stand, with a girl near them.
explanation.definitionFit: Where is the interrogative word used to ask about a place or location.

clue.text: This might draw in mostly nervous girl

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: windy is British slang for nervous or scared
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone might sketch a timid girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching, but here it means to haul; the definition is the whole phrase 'This might draw in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A windlass is a winch, a drum wound with rope or chain that hauls in loads or anchors.

clue.text: Returning stage of course to come together

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a course or journey

explanation.surface: A runner is coming back on one stretch of the race to meet the others.
explanation.definitionFit: When a team or plan gels, its parts set firmly together, as a jelly sets.

clue.text: Carry minute symbol of charm?

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Someone carries a tiny lucky token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective for small; it is the unit of time. The question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem with spiritual power, so it can be seen as a token of a magic charm.

clue.text: Go and hide, fink

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
an animal's hide is its coat

explanation.surface: An instruction to a sneak: leave and conceal yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' and 'hide' read as verbs but are nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: A fink is a slang term for an informer or traitor, and a turncoat is a person who betrays their side.

clue.text: Singer's evening at home with good beer

parts.note: night is evening
someone at home is in
G is the abbreviation for good
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A vocalist's night is spent indoors with a decent pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a performer, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for its rich song, often heard at night.

clue.text: Natter over a ciggie

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece goes on top

parts.note: to gas is to chatter or natter
per means a, as in once a day or once per day

explanation.surface: Chatting over a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette, like the informal ciggie.

clue.text: Unusual spirit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: odd or strange, in old-fashioned British slang
second meaning: a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: An odd ghost or an unusual drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a distilled drink and also dated British slang for something odd, as in 'a rum do'.

clue.text: In text you're caught by couple that's grown-up

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them
in text messages you're is shortened to these two letters

explanation.surface: A text message says you're grabbed by a pair who are adults.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mature is fully developed, an adult rather than a child.

clue.text: Flag in street is what you get at trattoria, say

definitions.text: what you get at trattoria, say

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street
to flag is to droop or sag

explanation.surface: A flag hanging in the street outside an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the verb meaning to tire, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian pasta dish, the kind served at a trattoria, a simple Italian restaurant; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Sell up what stands before hotel?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: flog is British slang for sell

explanation.surface: A hotel owner wants to sell off the land in front of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the word for G comes just before Hotel for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is the phonetic-alphabet word for G, which precedes Hotel, the word for H.

clue.text: Drop in ratings implies reduced cover above

parts.note: ratings are ordinary sailors, a ship's crew
a drop is a cut or reduction

explanation.surface: A fall in TV viewing figures suggests the programme's coverage was cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' suggests viewing figures; in Britain ratings are naval sailors below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, so the hair covering the head is reduced.

clue.text: Bread while in church

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
as means while, as in 'as I spoke'

explanation.surface: Bread is eaten during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not the communion loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and cash is money in notes and coins.

clue.text: Great source of oil found by son

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
oil is drawn from a well

explanation.surface: A son discovering an oil supply would be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is informal, chiefly American, for excellent or great.

clue.text: A place to relax in laid-back clubs — shock

parts.note: easy-going is laid-back
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: Relaxed nightclubs deliver a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a jolt, but it is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable armchair where one sits back and rests.
